### Notes

  with auto-defrag could keep tmpfs usage bounded.", "body_missing": false, "created_at": "2026-03-05T14:49:11Z", "id": 4005603719}, {"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "## etcd Storage Profiler - Run 3 (Full tmpfs Breakdown)

> PR [#84254](https://host-623.example/proj/proj/pull/84254) |
> Job [job-7504/2655601014204639343](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/84254/job-7504/2655601014204639343)

The virt-handler nsenter fix is working, **146 of 148 specs** now have full tmpfs/WAL/snap data.

### Final tmpfs Breakdown

| Component | Size | % of tmpfs used |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| **WAL dir** | **366.5 MB** | **72.6%** |
| Snap dir | 146.0 MB | 28.9% |
| DB file | 138.1 MB | 27.4% |
| DB in-use | 38.5 MB | (actual live data) |
| **Total tmpfs** | **504.7 MB / 1024 MB** | **49.3%** |
| **Peak tmpfs** | **519.5 MB / 1024 MB** | **50.7%** |

### Key Findings

#### WAL dominates tmpfs usage

WAL files consume **72.6%** of tmpfs. They grow in exact ~61 MB steps (etcd WAL segment size) and peaked at **427.4 MB** (7 segments) before a snapshot triggered cleanup:

| Spec | WAL Change | Trigger |
|------|------------|---------|
| 14 | 122.1 -> 183.1 MB (+61.0 MB) | [sig-compute] Infrastructure tls configuration should enforce TLS configuration  |
| 38 | 183.1 -> 244.1 MB (+61.0 MB) | [sig-compute]Configurations [rfe_id:92245][crit:medium][vendor:[email removed]] |
| 69 | 244.1 -> 305.2 MB (+61.0 MB) | [rfe_id:99072][crit:high][vendor:[email removed]][level:component][sig-compute]V |
| 81 | 305.2 -> 366.3 MB (+61.1 MB) | [sig-compute] Infrastructure cluster profiler for pprof data aggregation when Cl |
| 88 | 366.3 -> 427.4 MB (+61.1 MB) | [sig-compute] Infrastructure Node-labeller advanced labeling [test_id:98137] shou |
| 89 | 427.4 -> 366.4 MB (-61.0 MB) | [sig-compute] Infrastructure Node-labeller node with obsolete host-model cpuMode |

#### Snapshots accumulate steadily

Snapshot directory grew from 16 MB to 146 MB over the run in ~16 MB steps (one snapshot per step). etcd retains multiple snapshots before pruning old ones.

#### DB fragmentation remains significant

| Metric | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|
| Final DB size | 95.8 MB | 148.3 MB | 138.1 MB |
| Final DB in-use | 16.3 MB | 16.3 MB | 38.5 MB |
| Fragmentation | 83% | 89% | 72% |
| Final WAL | N/A | N/A | 366.5 MB |
| Final Snap | N/A | N/A | 146.0 MB |
| Final tmpfs | N/A | N/A | 504.7 MB |
| Peak tmpfs | N/A | N/A | 519.5 MB |

### Why the Old tmpfs Size Failed

With the default tmpfs (~512 MB), the suite would exceed capacity:
- WAL alone reaches ~366 MB (71% of 512 MB)
- Add DB (~138 MB) + snaps (~146 MB) and you are well past 100%
- The observed peak of 519.5 MB would have been fatal on a 512 MB tmpfs

### Root Cause

The problem is the combination of all three components growing together on tmpfs:
1. **WAL accumulates 6-7 segments** (~366-427 MB) before snapshot-triggered cleanup
2. **Snapshots accumulate** to ~146 MB (etcd retains multiple snapshots)
3. **DB file grows via fragmentation** to ~138 MB (only ~38 MB actually in use, no auto-defrag)

### Next Steps

1. **Compare `--snapshot-count`** between k8s 1.34 and 1.35 etcd static pod manifests - this controls WAL accumulation
2. **Check etcd version** bundled with k8s 1.35 vs 1.34 for default changes
3. **Run profiler on k8s 1.34 lane** to compare WAL/snap/DB growth patterns
4. Consider enabling `--auto-compaction-retention` and periodic `etcdctl defrag` to bound DB growth", "body_missing": false, "created_at": "2026-03-05T21:30:53Z", "id": 4007922717}, {"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "## Root Cause Found: etcd 3.6 `DefaultSnapshotCount` reduced 10x

### etcd version change across k8s releases

| | k8s 1.33 | k8s 1.34 | k8s 1.35 |
|--|----------|----------|----------|
| etcd version | 3.5.21 | 3.6.5 | 3.6.6 |
| `DefaultSnapshotCount` | **100,000** | **10,000** | **10,000** |

The [`DefaultSnapshotCount`](https://host-623.example/etcd-io/etcd/blob/v3.6.5/server/etcdserver/server.go#L74) was reduced from 100,000 to 10,000 in etcd 3.6, meaning etcd now takes a snapshot every 10K committed transactions instead of every 100K. This is a **10x increase in snapshot frequency**.

### How this causes tmpfs exhaustion

From our [Run 3 profiler data](#issuecomment-4007922717), the final tmpfs breakdown on a 1G tmpfs was:

| Component | Size | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| WAL dir | 366.5 MB | 6 segments × ~61 MB each |
| Snap dir | 146.0 MB | ~9 snapshot files × ~16 MB each |
| DB file | 138.1 MB | Only 38.5 MB in-use, rest is fragmentation |
| **Total** | **504.7 MB** | **Peak was 519.5 MB** |

With 10x more frequent snapshots:
- More snapshot files accumulate before old ones are pruned (~9 retained at ~16 MB each = 146 MB)
- WAL segments rotate faster but more accumulate between snapshot-triggered cleanup (up to 7 segments = 427 MB at peak)
- The previous default tmpfs of **512 MB** (set by [projci](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/056f8f79/cluster-provision/gocli/opts/etcd/etcd.go#L18)) is too small for this workload under etcd 3.6

### projci kubeadm configs are identical

The [k8s 1.34](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/056f8f79/cluster-provision/k8s/1.34/manifests/kubeadm.conf) and [k8s 1.35](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/056f8f79/cluster-provision/k8s/1.35/manifests/kubeadm.conf) kubeadm configs are identical — neither sets `--snapshot-count` or any other etcd extra args. The changed default comes purely from the etcd binary version bundled with k8s 1.34+.

### Possible fixes

1. **Keep the 1G tmpfs workaround** (current state via [project-infra#83138](https://host-623.example/proj/project-infra/pull/83138)) — simplest, provides ~2x headroom
2. **Increase `--snapshot-count` back to 100000** in kubeadm.conf for projci providers — restores previous behavior but fights upstream defaults
3. **Bump the projci default tmpfs** from 512M to 1G for all etcd-in-memory providers — fixes it for everyone, not just sig-compute-serial
4. **Enable `--auto-compaction-retention`** to keep DB fragmentation bounded — helps but doesn't address WAL/snap growth which is the larger contributor

Option 3 seems like the right long-term fix since all etcd-in-memory lanes on k8s 1.34+ will be affected, not just sig-compute-serial.", "body_missing": false, "created_at": "2026-03-05T21:35:58Z", "id": 4007946429}, {"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "/cc @person-56de3185

{"author": "person-71d578da", "body": "## Problem

Since we updated to Fedora 39 we see increased console-connection
flakes against VMs in CI. The image is now also stale (F39 is EOL) and
no longer receiving updates.

CI search links:
- [120s timeout flakes](https://host-498.example/?search=expect%3A+timer+expired+after+120+seconds&maxAge=336h&context=1&type=bug%2Bjunit&name=&excludeName=&maxMatches=5&maxBytes=20971520&groupBy=job)
- [30s timeout flakes](https://host-498.example/?search=expect%3A+timer+expired+after+30+seconds&maxAge=336h&context=1&type=bug%2Bjunit&name=&excludeName=&maxMatches=5&maxBytes=20971520&groupBy=job)

## Root cause

The regression has multiple contributing factors. Below are some of the
reasons and directions we have identified so far:

- Several tests open a console to the VM **before** the
  `GuestAgentConnected` event fires. The guest-agent ready event is a
  healthier gate because it implies cloud-init has finished and the VM is
  fully initialised. Connecting earlier is inherently less stable.
- Other timing-related issues may also play a role, but fixing the
  guest-agent gating should reduce the noise enough to isolate them.

## Recommendation

1. **Bump the Fedora image first.** Upgrading to the latest supported
   Fedora gives us a current baseline and eliminates noise from F39-specific
   quirks. Any flakes that remain after the bump are the real bugs to fix.
EDIT - i am on it, PRs are open (WIP), it also disabled `pam_nologin`
https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/76719
https://host-623.example/proj/proj/pull/96658

2. **Gate console access on `GuestAgentConnected`.** Aligning the remaining
   tests to wait for the guest-agent event before opening a console should
   remove the main source of instability.
3. **Triage residual flakes.** With a fresh image and the gating fix in
   place, the remaining failures will be easier to isolate and address
   one at a time.

### Root Cause

The `BeforeEach` patches the Proj CR to set `uninstallStrategy: BlockUninstallIfWorkloadsExist`, then only waits for the *spec* to reflect the change. It does not wait for the virt-operator to finish reconciling after the patch.

The patch triggers a full operator reconciliation (hundreds of resource updates — CRDs, RBAC, services, webhooks, certificates, configmaps) which saturates the kube-apiserver. The test then immediately creates a VMI, which goes through the virt-api validating webhook. The apiserver cannot complete the webhook round-trip within the 10s deadline because it is busy processing the operator's update requests.

Artifact analysis from [a representative failure](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/72616/job-4614/6374269226189553592) confirms:
- **virt-api pods were healthy** — both running, 0 restarts, serving HTTP 200s
- **kube-apiserver was overloaded** — logged "client disconnected" and "Handler timeout" errors at 14:35:03 UTC
- **virt-operator was mid-reconciliation** — all deployments and the virt-handler DaemonSet were rolling at the time of failure
- **Proj CR status**: `Available=True` (reason: `UpdateInProgress`), `Progressing=True`, `Degraded=True`

# Flake Action Plan

Revealed a real bug. VM force restart is performed by the virt-api and it includes two steps:
1. Sending PATCH to VM status `stateChangeRequests` with `Stop` and `Start`
2. Sending DELETE call to the VMI pod with grace period of 1 second

The race condition happens between step 1 and 2, The VM conttoller reconciles the VM state and stops the VMI, the VMI controller in turn reconciles the VMI and deletes the VMI pod. 
Because of the [following](https://host-623.example/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93928) kubelet limitation, the `StopContainer` action performed by kubelet and CRI-O is blocking. It means that if the VMI controller fires the pod deletion before virt-api, the grace period of 1 second isn't being honored during the delete call from virt-api. 

In the test scenario the `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is being set with 600 seconds. From the k8s-reporter artifacts it can be seen that the pod `virt-launcher-testvmi-2pgv4-jfl5b` of the VM `testvmi-2pgv4`
is stuck in `Terminating` phase, causing the test to fail. Pod metadata has `deletionGracePeriodSeconds` label set to `1` which means that pod deletion with grace period 1 indeed received by the k8s API server.

## Additional context

`runOverlayQMPSession` in `pkg/component-547/virtwrap/storage/cbt.go` uses a `select` on three channels: `concludedChan`, `scanDone`, and `ctx.Done()`. When the scanner goroutine reads from an in-memory `strings.NewReader` (as in the unit test), it finds the `concluded` event and closes `concludedChan`, then immediately hits EOF and closes `scanDone`. Both channels become ready at essentially the same time.

Go's `select` picks a random ready case when multiple are available, so it non-deterministically chooses `scanDone` over `concludedChan`, causing the spurious error:

```
qemu-storage-daemon exited without job concluding for overlay /test/overlay.qcow2
```

### CI search results

Searching for `exited without job concluding` over the last 14 days found **3 matches** in `job-6610` out of 445 total runs, accounting for ~5% of the 61 failed runs in that job.

### Fix

The fix adds a nested non-blocking check on `concludedChan` inside the `scanDone` case, giving it priority — the standard Go idiom for channel priority in a `select`:

```go
case <-scanDone:
    select {
    case <-concludedChan:
        fmt.Fprintf(stdin, "%s\n%s\n%s\n", queryJobs, jobDismiss, quit)
    default:
        err = fmt.Errorf("qemu-storage-daemon exited without job concluding for overlay %s", overlayPath)
    }
```

# Flake Action Plan

### The flake is a bug

## Failure Details

### 1. DomainNotifyServer - should be resilient to notify server restarts

**File:** `pkg/component-261/launcher-clients/launcher-clients_test.go:220`

```
[FAILED] Unexpected error: context deadline exceeded
```

The test repeatedly restarts a notify server and expects the client to reconnect within tight timeouts (1s connect, 3s overall). On arm64, the reconnection loop hits `connect: no such file or directory` errors while the server is restarting, and the `context deadline exceeded` before a successful connection can be made.

This is a recurrence of #47123 which was previously closed as rotten.

### 2. AccessCredentials - should support multiple ssh keys in one secret value

**File:** `pkg/component-547/virtwrap/access-credentials/access_credentials_test.go:281`

```
[FAILED] Timed out after 5.000s. Expected <chan struct {} | len:0, cap:0> to be closed
```

The test waits for an `Eventually` with a 5-second timeout for a channel to be closed after SSH key propagation. On arm64, the mock-based credential handling does not complete within this window.

## Root Cause

Both failures are caused by timeouts that are too tight for the arm64 CI environment. The arm64 unit test job likely runs under emulation or on constrained hardware, making these timing-sensitive tests unreliable.

## Additional context

- PR #82938 is unrelated to both test areas (it quarantines a sig-scale test), confirming these are pre-existing flakes.
- The DomainNotifyServer flake was previously reported as #47123 and closed as rotten without a fix.

This looks like a gap in how KinD providers set up storage for CDI. The root cause is that CDI's StorageProfile auto-detection doesn't properly populate `accessModes` for the `rancher.io/local-path` provisioner used by KinD, while on the regular K8s provider the `host-860.example/no-provisioner` with the local-volume-provisioner DaemonSet works correctly [[1]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-up/cluster/kind/manifests/local-storage-class.yaml) [[2]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-provision/k8s/1.33/manifests/local-volume.yaml).

When CDI deploys on a KinD cluster, it creates a StorageProfile for the `local` StorageClass but fails to populate its `claimPropertySets` with `accessModes`, leading to the `no accessMode specified in StorageProfile local` error when DataVolumes are created [[3]](https://host-623.example/proj/proj/blob/84ff809176232d94d4f3ae90edab4e6a8a96ace3/pkg/component-328/types/cdi.go#L39-L41).

There's prior work in projci that explicitly added the `local` StorageClass manifest for KinD [[4]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461), but no equivalent step creates or patches the StorageProfile with the required `accessModes`. A similar approach could fix this — adding an explicit StorageProfile manifest to the KinD cluster-up scripts [[5]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-up/cluster/kind/common.sh#L267-L271).

**Immediate workaround**: After `make cluster-up` and CDI deployment, patch the StorageProfile:

```yaml
apiVersion: cdi.proj.example/v1beta1
kind: StorageProfile
metadata:
  name: local
spec:
  claimPropertySets:
  - accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
    volumeMode: Filesystem
```

**Long-term fix**: The KinD provider's cluster-up scripts in projci should be updated to create/patch the `local` StorageProfile with appropriate `claimPropertySets` after CDI is deployed, similar to how the `local` StorageClass manifest was explicitly added in [projci PR #85461](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461) [[6]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461).

You can verify the current state with:

```bash
kubectl get storageprofile local -o jsonpath='{.status.claimPropertySets}'
```

If this returns empty/null, that confirms the issue.

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

The `virt-exportproxy` pod in the `proj` namespace panics and enters **CrashLoopBackOff**, causing 24 cascading serial test failures in `job-9845`.

## Failing Job

- **Job**: [job-9845 / 3059281404328236697](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/logs/job-9845/3059281404328236697)
- **Date**: 2026-04-24
- **Result**: 517 Passed | 26 Failed | 4 Pending | 833 Skipped (suite timeout elapsed)

## Root Cause

The `virt-exportproxy` container panics early in the test run. The build log detects:

```
ERROR: Found panic in test output
Files:
/logs/artifacts/k8s-reporter/1/pods/2_proj_virt-exportproxy-6cd5b869cd-8qvrw-exportproxy.log
/logs/artifacts/k8s-reporter/1/pods/2_proj_virt-exportproxy-6cd5b869cd-8qvrw-exportproxy_previous.log
```

The restart count escalates throughout the run:

| Snapshot | Restarts | BackOff Events |
|---|---|---|
| process=1/failure=2 | 9 | 27 |
| process=1/failure=3 | 11 | 33 |
| process=1/failure=5 | 15 | 59 |
| suite/failure=0 | **35** | **160** |

## Cascading Failures

All 24 serial test failures share the same pattern — they fail in `[AfterEach]` at `tests/component-779/fixture.go:44920` with:

```
Timed out after 300.000s.
One of the Proj control-plane components is not ready.
Expected condition of type 'Available' and status 'True' but got 'False'
```

The AfterEach cleanup asserts that all Proj control plane components are healthy. Since `virt-exportproxy` is perpetually crashing, every serial test that runs after the crash started fails on cleanup.

### Affected test areas (all Serial)

- Control plane resilience (pod eviction, PDB, connectivity) — `virt_control_plane_test.go`
- CPU pinning (8 tests with cpu-manager) — `vmi_configuration_test.go`
- EFI bootloader, machine type, chassis value, custom PCI addresses
- TLS configuration, runtime class, guest-to-request memory

## Additional Cluster Issues (likely consequences)

- **virt-handler**: 10 `Unhealthy` events — readiness probe returning HTTP 500
- **virt-api**: 4 `FailedScheduling` events — `0/2 nodes are available: 2 node(s) were unschedulable`
- **VMI stuck in Scheduled phase**: `testvmi-cp9tr` in `proj-test-default2` never reached Running

## Suggested Investigation

1. Check the panic stack trace in the exportproxy container logs (linked above in the GCS artifacts)
2. Determine if this is a new regression or a known flake
3. Consider whether the AfterEach timeout (300s) is sufficient given a crashing component, or if the test framework should detect CrashLoopBackOff earlier and skip remaining serial tests

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

The test `[sig-storage] Volumes update with migration Hotplug volumes should be able to volume migrate a VM with a datavolume and an hotplugged datavolume migrating from block to filesystem` is failing at a ~21% rate on k8s 1.36, while it is stable (0% failure) on k8s 1.34 and 1.35.

## Failure Rate (from testgrid)

| Lane (k8s version) | Failure Rate | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **k8s 1.36** sig-storage | **21.4% (12/56 runs)** | Flaky |
| **k8s 1.35** sig-storage | **0.0% (0/225 runs)** | Stable |
| **k8s 1.34** sig-storage | **0.0% (0/42409 runs)** | Stable |

### Related test variants on k8s 1.36

| Migration direction | Failure Rate |
|---|---|
| block → filesystem | **21.4%** (worst) |
| filesystem → filesystem | **8.9%** |
| block → block | 0% |
| filesystem → block | 0% |

Pattern: migrations **targeting filesystem** volumes are affected on k8s 1.36 only. Migrations targeting block storage are stable.

## Root Cause (from build 3309147724183903808)

The destination PVC ends up with **0 bytes** allocated, causing QEMU to fail immediately:

```
Volume migration cannot be performed because the destination volume is smaller than the source volume:
virError(Code=1, Domain=10, Message='internal error: process exited while connecting to monitor:
qemu-kvm: -blockdev {"driver":"raw","file":"libvirt-1-storage","offset":0,"size":1000341504,
"node-name":"libvirt-1-slice-sto","read-only":false,"discard":"unmap","cache":{"direct":true,
"no-flush":false}}: The sum of offset (0) and size (1000341504) has to be smaller or equal to
the actual size of the containing file (0)')
```

K8s cluster events from the failing run show:
- **ClaimMisbound**: two claims bound to the same PV
- **ProvisioningFailed**: conflict error saving the PVC
- **FailedScheduling**: importer pod has unbound immediate PVCs
- 25x **MigrationBackoff** followed by 360s timeout

This suggests a PVC provisioning/binding race condition that is specific to k8s 1.36.

- Failure line: https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/logs/job-1952/3309147724183903808#1:build-log.txt%3A7610

### What this PR does

Motivation:
Every error in virt-launcher logs represents a potential bug or issue in the system. 
Until now, passing tests could silently leave behind unexpected errors in VM logs, 
allowing bugs to slip through undetected.
This PR ensures we catch and prevent new issues from being introduced.

This PR adds automated VM log validation to the e2e test suite. 
When a test passes, we now validate that virt-launcher logs contain no unexpected errors,
if any are found, the test fails.

Allowlist-First Approach:
We start by allowlisting current known errors.
This establishes a baseline.
Follow-up efforts can validate each allowelisted error and fix them as needed. 
The purpose of this PR is to introduce the mechanism and prevent regression.

Note:
We can also introduce incremental approach, where each sig will update the list and enable the feature on it's lane.
We can also split the list into topics or even list per sig for easier maintenance.
If desired i can suggest a follow-up VEP for it.

Standalone Tool:
The validation logic is also available as a standalone binary (`vmlog-checker`) for local development and debugging.
Run it on logs to see categorized output with color-coding, or use `--errors-only` to see just the problems.
This makes it easy to test allowlist updates or investigate failures, since the known errors are already labeled.

Idea of @person-d131fbd8 

```
tests/vmlogchecker/              ← LIB: classification logic + allowlist
├── vmlog_checker.go
└── vmlog_checker_test.go
        │
        ├──► tools/vmlog-checker/    ← STANDALONE CLI: offline log analysis
        │    └── main.go               developer tool
        │
        └──► tests/component-630/         ← E2E INTEGRATION: live test validation
             └── vmlog_reporter.go     checks virt-launcher logs after each test
```

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
virt-launcher scanned all metadata files in a flat directory to find attributes for DRA devices, because the system-generated ResourceClaim name for template claims was not available at lookup time.

#### After this PR:
Adopts the KEP-5304 directory layout for DRA device metadata. Metadata is now read from structured paths `/var/run/host-860.example/dra-device-attributes/{resourceclaims,resourceclaimtemplates}/<claimName>/<requestName>/<driverName>-metadata.json`, using the pod-level claim name for templates so no scanning is needed. 

Metadata files are decoded as versioned JSON streams, skipping unsupported API versions for forward compatibility with newer drivers. 

Additionally, the DRA admitter validation is refactored to de-duplicate GPU and HostDevice checks, and error handling for unresolvable devices is improved.

{"author": "person-7e8bec95", "base": "main", "body": "Flake 1: console login after the VM migrates flakes
Example: https://host-586.example/view/gcs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/54095/job-2650/8782299347731493766
This PR This removes the console login step altogether.
In a real scenario the user may not want to configure the guest IP after updating the NAD. If both the static VMIs have the same subnet there would be no need to reconfigure the IP of the migrating VMI. 

Flake 2: ping after migration fails
Example: https://host-586.example/view/gcs/proj-prow/logs/job-9338/8371082394952303408

This PR makes sure that the migrating VM has completed its migration before fetching the node it is running on.  This node is later used to spawn the second VMI to verify connectivity.
Currently the node info is fetched just after migrationRequired condition disappears. This does not guarantee that migration has already happened and so sometimes the node info of the source VM is fetched. As
a result the second VMI is spawned on the source node rather than target node and the ping fails.
We see that in the logs:

{"author": "person-2368fae2", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
During live migration the QEMU guest agent is temporarily unreachable on two different pods depending on the migration phase: 
- Pre-copy: the target pod has the guest paused while receiving memory pages — a GuestAgentPing probe there produces false negatives, causing Kubernetes to restart the target pod and abort the migration.
- Post-copy: the source VM is handed off to the target and enters a ghost/paused state — the same probe on the source pod produces false negatives, again risking a pod restart.

Because GuestAgentPing is implemented as a Kubernetes exec probe running inside each pod's compute container, kubelet executes it on both pods simultaneously throughout the migration. Both failure modes could abort an in-progress migration.  

More generally, whenever a VM is paused by the user or by the platform for an intentional reason (snapshot, save, dump, …) the guest agent is also unreachable, and a GuestAgentPing liveness probe would kill the pod.

#### After this PR:
This PR is split into two commits that can be cherry-picked independently to release branches.

Commit 1 - migration (MVP): `LibvirtDomainManager.GuestPing` suppresses probe errors for the duration of an in-progress migration on any pod where they occur. The check is intentionally simple: if migration metadata has `StartTimestamp` set and no EndTimestamp, a migration is in progress and any probe failure is returned as a synthetic success. No attempt is made to distinguish source from target, the suppression path is only reached when the probe has already failed, which only happens when the guest is genuinely unreachable. The suppression window closes as soon as EndTimestamp is set, after which the real guest-agent ping resumes normally.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                  
Commit 2 - healthy paused states: When no migration is in progress, GuestPing falls back to a new `isPausedButHealthy` helper that inspects the libvirt domain pause reason via the API. Suppression is applied for an explicit allowlist of intentional/transient pause reasons (user pause, snapshot, save, dump, postcopy, …). Fault pauses (IOError, Crashed, PostcopyFailed) are intentionally excluded so genuine guest problems are still surfaced. An allowlist is preferred over a denylist so that unknown future libvirt pause reasons default to not being suppressed.

Other probe types (exec, httpGet, tcpSocket) are intentionally left unchanged — their semantics during migration are consistent with regular Kubernetes pods and are tuneable via initialDelaySeconds/failureThreshold.

Documentation updated in docs/probes.md and in the GuestAgentPing API comment. Unit tests cover all migration-phase/pod-role combinations and every healthy and unhealthy pause reason. E2e regression tests cover both the migration case and the user-pause case.

### References
- Partially addresses https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/pull/35133

Jira-ticket: https://host-696.example/browse/TICKET-342619

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
The following tradeoffs were made:

The following alternatives were considered:
proj/enhancements#35133 is proposing an annotation-driven mechanism to dynamically pause arbitrary probes. A similar approach will try to solve a problem that does not exist for standard Kubernetes probe types (exec, httpGet, tcpSocket), which already have initialDelaySeconds and failureThreshold as the intended knobs.
I tend to think that the problem could be narrowly defined: GuestAgentPing is the only VM specific probe type and its failure during an incoming migration is a structural impossibility rather than a real fault; the guest OS simply cannot reply because it is still running on the source node.
A generic annotation-driven pause just for VMs would introduce new API surface and operational complexity for a failure mode that can be handled transparently and automatically at the right abstraction layer.

The two commits are intentionally independent so that only the first (migration suppression) can be cherry-picked to release branches if the second (healthy paused states) is considered too broad for a backport.

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

The `BlockUninstallIfWorkloadsExist` `BeforeEach` calls `allKvInfraPodsAreReady` and `sanityCheckDeploymentsExist` before patching the Proj CR. This catches any pending reconciliation from the previous test's `AfterEach` but does not wait for the reconciliation triggered by the `BeforeEach` patch itself. The `AfterEach` also doesn't wait for reconciliation after removing the uninstall strategy.

This means the test can attempt to create a VMI while the operator is still reconciling, saturating the kube-apiserver and causing the virt-api webhook to timeout.

#### After this PR:

- `BeforeEach`: `allKvInfraPodsAreReady` and `sanityCheckDeploymentsExist` are moved from before the patch to after it, so they wait for the reconciliation triggered by setting the uninstall strategy.
- `AfterEach`: `allKvInfraPodsAreReady` and `sanityCheckDeploymentsExist` are added after removing the uninstall strategy, ensuring reconciliation completes before the next test cycle.

### References

- Fixes #63169

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The flake has **21 hits across 4 sig-operator jobs in the last 14 days**. Artifact analysis of [a representative failure](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/72616/job-4614/6374269226189553592) confirmed:

- virt-api pods were healthy (running, 0 restarts, serving HTTP 200s)
- The kube-apiserver logged "client disconnected" and "Handler timeout" errors during the failure
- The virt-operator was mid-reconciliation with all deployments and the virt-handler DaemonSet rolling

### Special notes for your reviewer

Both `BeforeEach` and `AfterEach` patch the Proj CR, each triggering an operator reconciliation. Both now wait for reconciliation to complete with `allKvInfraPodsAreReady` and `sanityCheckDeploymentsExist` after their respective patches.

{"author": "person-4c34b631", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does

When a migration completes successfully, the source domain transitions to Shutoff/Migrated and the migrate() function returns, closing migrationErrorChan. 
The monitor goroutine's select then returns immediately on every iteration (reading nil from a closed channel), and GetJobStats(0) fails because the domain is inactive. The original code logged a warning and called continue, creating a busy loop that spins at 100% CPU for the lifetime of the virt-launcher pod.
Fix this by simplifying the monitor loop by removing the inconsequential handling of various errors and calling GetJobStats(0) unconditionally each iteration, and enhance logMigrationInfo to show actual Downtime/DowntimeNet (instead of ExpectedDowntime) when completed job data is available. The completed job is not queried at all, instead an async event carries all the data and logs them.

Assisted-by: claude-4.6-opus

#### Before this PR:

on successful migration there's a 100% CPU busy loop until the pod dies, spamming log and causing more libvirt contention

#### After this PR:

no more log flood, more accurate final stats information

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
The select in `runOverlayQMPSession` treated `concludedChan` and `scanDone` as mutually exclusive outcomes but both can fire on every successful run. When the scanner finishes before the select observes `concludedChan`, cleanup commands are never sent and a false error is reported.

#### After this PR:
This PR replaces the goroutine with `errgroup` to consolidate scan error handling and adds a priority check so `concludedChan` is always observed when the job does conclude.

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
virt-handler currently mounts /var/lib/kubelet with MountPropagationBidirectional. When other components on the node (e.g. CSI pods) also mount child directories such as /var/lib/kubelet/plugins or /var/lib/kubelet/pods as bidirectional, each restart of virt-handler doubles the mount count on the node due to the bidirectional propagation preserving old mounts while creating new ones. After 10-12 restarts this causes the node to become unusable with "device or resource busy" errors from kubelet/containerd.

Bidirectional propagation on this volume is unnecessary because:

Hotplug disk operations use virt-chroot with /proc/1/root to operate directly in the host mount namespace
Device plugin registration only needs read/write socket access
Seccomp profile installation only writes files
cpu_manager_state is read-only

#### After this PR:
Change the kubelet volume mount propagation from Bidirectional to HostToContainer, which still allows virt-handler to see new mounts created by kubelet on the host, while preventing mount explosion from container-to-host propagation.

{"author": "person-6a66b511", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

`AdjustDomainForTopologyAndCPUSet` dereferences `domain.Spec.VCPUs.VCPU` when `vmi.Spec.Domain.CPU.MaxSockets != 0`, without checking whether `domain.Spec.VCPUs` is nil first.

`domain.Spec.VCPUs` is a `*VCPUs` pointer (populated by `domainVCPUTopologyForHotplug` only when hotplug is supported) and is **not set** in at least one call path:

- `cpudedicated.go:AdjustCPUDedicated` builds a `domain` with `CPU.Topology` and `VCPU` (singular), but never initializes `VCPUs` (plural). When called for a VMI with `MaxSockets > 0`, virt-launcher panics with a nil pointer dereference.

The same risk exists when `AdjustDomainForTopologyAndCPUSet` is called from `manager.go` during live vCPU hotplug if the libvirt domain XML lacks a `<vcpus>` element.

#### After this PR:

The condition is extended to `MaxSockets != 0 && domain.Spec.VCPUs != nil`, so the disabled-socket adjustment is skipped when VCPU metadata is absent.
This is safe because if `VCPUs` is nil, there are no disabled VCPUs to subtract from the requested topology.

### References
<!-- optional,
  Use `Fixes #<issue number>(, Fixes #<issue_number>, ...)` format, to close the issue(s) when PR gets merged.
  Use `Partially addresses #<issue number>` to link an issue without closing it when the PR merges.
  

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The fix is a single nil guard added to the existing condition.
Alternatives considered:

- Initializing `VCPUs` in `cpudedicated.go` before calling `AdjustDomainForTopologyAndCPUSet` — rejected because populating dummy VCPU entries would be incorrect and couple the caller to internal hotplug logic.
- Moving the nil check inside the loop body — rejected because skipping the entire block when there is no VCPU metadata is the correct semantic (no VCPUs metadata = no disabled VCPUs = nothing to adjust).

{"author": "person-d92002c6", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does

The `docs/devel/networking.md` file has drifted significantly from the
codebase over time, accumulating several categories of inaccuracy.
This PR corrects them and relocates the file to a more appropriate home.

**Removing SLIRP.** The SLIRP binding was removed from Proj but the
documentation still mentioned it in two places, which is misleading for
anyone reading it to understand the current system.

**Decoupling from the implementation.** The document described the
networking phases by naming specific Go methods, interface definitions,
and an internal file path for the VIF cache. This tight coupling means
the doc goes stale every time the implementation is refactored, even
when the logical behavior is unchanged. Replacing method names with
abstract descriptions of what each phase achieves makes the document
durable across code changes.

**Clarifying hypervisor-specific content.** Domain XML snippets are
specific to the libvirt/QEMU hypervisor. The document presented them as
universal truth. A clear callout was added so readers understand these
are implementation details of one hypervisor and may differ for others.

**Fixing the dummy interface description.** The document incorrectly
stated that a dummy NIC is created in masquerade binding to prevent MAC
address inheritance. A review of `pkg/component-330/setup` showed the opposite
is true: the dummy interface is created in bridge binding (not
masquerade), where it takes the original pod interface name and preserves
the original MAC, IPs, MTU, and routes. It serves two distinct purposes:
first, the in-pod DHCP server uses it in phase 2 to advertise the correct
addressing to the VM, effectively carrying the pod IP into the guest;
second, it allows the container runtime to continue answering CNI CHECK
commands at runtime — since the pod IP is moved to the guest and removed
from the renamed pod interface, the dummy retains it so CNI can still
verify the pod network configuration is intact. Masquerade binding does
not create a dummy interface at all.

**Replacing the external diagram.** The bridge binding diagram was hosted
externally on proj.github.io, making it impossible to review or
update as part of a PR to this repo. It also contained two factual errors:
the group containing vnet0 and br1 was labeled "Configured by Libvirt"
(it is configured by virt-handler), and the DHCP component was labeled
as simply "DHCP" with no indication of who configures it. The diagram has
been replaced with a versioned SVG stored in the repo, with corrected
labels. The eth0 pod interface is now shown as shared between the
virt-handler group and the CNI group (visually indicated by two distinct
overlapping borders), reflecting that CNI initially configures it before
virt-handler modifies it.

**Relocating the file.** `docs/devel/` is a general developer area,
while `docs/network/` already exists and holds network-specific developer
documentation. Moving the file there, with a more descriptive name
(`network-binding-mechanisms.md`), makes it easier to discover alongside
related content.

### References

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Documentation that names internal symbols (methods, types, file paths)
creates a maintenance trap: any refactor that renames those symbols
silently invalidates the doc, and the doc gives reviewers no warning.
Keeping the description at the logical level — what each phase does,
not how it is implemented — means the document remains accurate as long
as the behavior is unchanged.

The following tradeoffs were made:

Replacing the PNG with an SVG means the diagram is now a text file,
diff-able and reviewable in PRs. The trade-off is that SVG is more
verbose to edit by hand than a GUI tool, but this is acceptable for a
diagram that changes infrequently.

The following alternatives were considered:

A Mermaid diagram was considered as a replacement for the SVG. It was
ruled out because Mermaid does not support a node belonging to two
subgroups simultaneously, which is needed to show that eth0 is configured
by both CNI and virt-handler.

### What this PR does
This PR Fixes two issues in hack/cluster-clean.sh that cause the cleanup to hang or fail.
The s390x periodic E2E Test lane is failing at the cluster-cleanup 
https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/logs/job-4618/2641036934633935585
```
20:40:45: + echo 'waiting for cluster-clean to finish'
20:40:45: waiting for cluster-clean to finish
20:40:45: + wait 11864
```
The cluster clean is not able to clean up the left over proj resources. The  Proj's validatingwebhookconfiguration and mutatingwebhookconfiguration are blocking the proj from deleting it.
This is the state of the proj during the time of the error.
```
root@projci-s390x-external-controlplane:~# kubectl get all -n proj
NAME                            AGE   PHASE
proj.proj.example/proj   10h   Deleting
root@projci-s390x-external-controlplane:~# kubectl get kv proj -n proj -o jsonpath='{.metadata.finalizers}'
["host-215.example/foregroundDeleteProj"]root@projci-s390x-external-controlplane:~# 
root@projci-s390x-external-controlplane:~# 
root@projci-s390x-external-controlplane:~# kubectl patch kv proj -n proj --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/metadata/finalizers"}]'
Error from server (Internal Error): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "proj-update-validator.proj.example": failed to call webhook: Post "[https://host-943.example:443/proj-validate-update?timeout=10s](https://host-943.example/proj-validate-update?timeout=10s)": service "proj-operator-webhook" not foundDue to the validating webhook the finalizer removal on proj is failed. 
```

Later the script proceeds to the step to delete the pods,crds etc and there it hung. So, it waited for the cluster-clean to finish and eventually the prow job timed out.

#### Before this PR:

- The Proj CR gets stuck in Deleting because the validating webhook blocks finalizer removal after the backing service is already gone.

#### After this PR:

- Webhook registrations (validating and mutating) are deleted after the graceful KV CR delete attempt but before the finalizer patch, so the patch is no longer blocked.

{"author": "person-4c34b631", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

Commit e9107af007 ("fix: initialize migration cache on the target", PR #96567) added `initializeMigrationMetadata()` to `prepareMigrationTarget` to fix a `StartTimestamp` race. However, it also copied the `if inProgress { return nil }` guard from the source-side `startMigration`. On the target side, if `prepareMigrationTarget` fails *after* storing the metadata (e.g. at the functional-test annotation check, or any later step), the retry finds metadata already present, concludes "inProgress", and returns `nil` -- silently skipping the rest of preparation (cloud-init ISO, hooks, migration socket setup). This causes QEMU to crash on the target ("Failed to bind socket ... No such file or directory").

`test_id:6980` ("Migration should fail if target pod fails during target preparation") is flaky because of this -- the annotation block succeeds on the first call but the immediate retry bypasses it via the `inProgress` short-circuit.

#### After this PR:

The `inProgress` return value is ignored on the target side. The metadata is still initialized (preserving the `StartTimestamp` fix from #96567), but the full preparation always runs. Re-preparation is already guarded at the virt-handler level by `GetTargetListenerPorts` and `IsMigrating` checks in `processVMI`, so the `inProgress` guard is redundant here.

### References

- Root cause: commit e9107af007 merged via #96567
- Flake observed in: https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj%5Fproj/71051/job-9794/5362113304475248449

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The `inProgress` guard in `initializeMigrationMetadata` is semantically correct on the **source** side: it prevents spawning a duplicate QEMU migration goroutine if `startMigration` is called multiple times. On the **target** side it has no such role -- `prepareMigrationTarget` is a synchronous RPC that must complete fully. If any step after `initializeMigrationMetadata` fails, virt-handler retries via `AddRateLimited`, which calls `prepareMigrationTarget` again within milliseconds. The retry then hits the `inProgress` early-return and silently succeeds without setting up migration sockets, causing QEMU to crash.

The fix simply ignores the `inProgress` return on the target path. No tradeoffs -- the metadata initialization is preserved, and higher-level guards prevent true double-preparation.

### Special notes for your reviewer

One-line change. The `initializeMigrationMetadata` call is preserved (its side effect of storing the metadata is still needed), only the `inProgress` early-return is removed.

- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future contributors
- [x] Code: Write code that humans can understand and Keep it simple
- [x] Testing: Existing `test_id:6980` covers this scenario -- it should stop flaking with this fix
- [x] AI Contributions: The PR abides by the Proj AI Contribution Policy.

#### Before this PR:
  GuestPanicked events show "details unavailable" for non-root virt-launcher pods:                                                                            
``` 
Warning   GuestPanicked   virtualmachineinstance/windows-vm   GuestPanicked (details unavailable)
```

#### After this PR:
  GuestPanicked events show actual Windows bugcheck codes:                                                                                                    
```

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
  The VMI object created with `NewVMIReferenceWithUUID()` doesn't set `Status.RuntimeUser`, causing `vmitrait.IsNonRoot()` to return false. This leads to using the wrong log path and failing to read panic details.                                                                                                 
                                                            
  The fix passes the runWithNonRoot flag through the call chain `startDomainEventMonitoring → StartDomainNotifier → eventCallback → handleGuestPanicEvent` so it's used directly to determine the correct log path, instead of relying on the VMI object's status.

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

The `waitRunningVMI` helper used strict `Equal(vmiCount)` to assert the number of running VMIs. The primer VMI created in `BeforeEach` may or may not still be running when batch tests check the count. This caused flakes regardless of the expected count:

- With `vmCount+1` (101): failed when the primer was evicted → `"Expected 100 to equal 101"`
- With `vmCount` (100) (after #32007): failed when the primer survived → `"Expected 101 to equal 100"` (more common, making the flake rate worse)

#### After this PR:

Uses `BeNumerically(">=", vmiCount)` so the assertion passes whether the primer VMI is still running (101 >= 100) or has been evicted (100 >= 100).

### References

- Fixes #32849
- Follow-up to #32007

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
The following tradeoffs were made:
- Using `>=` rather than exact equality means we won't catch a hypothetical bug that creates extra VMIs, but the test's purpose is to verify density/performance (all batch VMIs reach Running), not exact VMI accounting.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Deleting the primer VMI before running batch tests — more invasive and changes the test's warm-up semantics.
- Filtering out the primer VMI by name when counting — adds complexity for no real benefit.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The fix in #32007 changed the expected count from `vmCount+1` to `vmCount`, which inverted the failure condition. Since the primer VMI surviving is more common than being evicted, the flake rate actually increased after that change. Periodic job data showed 4/5 post-fix runs failing vs 1/5 pre-fix.

{"author": "person-bf460e3a", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

`addNamespacedResourceAttributes()` uses `pathSplit[8]` to extract the subresource from the URL path, capturing only the first segment. Deep subresources like `vnc/screenshot`, `sev/fetchcertchain`, and `evacuate/cancel` are truncated to `vnc`, `sev`, `evacuate` - causing the SAR to check authorization against the wrong (broader) subresource name.

#### After this PR:

All remaining path segments are joined into the subresource name. For `portforward`, where trailing segments are dynamic parameters (port, protocol), only `portforward` is used. Single-segment subresources are unaffected.

### References

- Fixes #57935

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The SAR subresource must match the RBAC resource names defined in `pkg/component-611/resource/generate/rbac/cluster.go` (e.g. `virtualmachineinstances/vnc/screenshot`, `virtualmachineinstances/sev/fetchcertchain`). The truncation causes a mismatch between the authorization check and the actual RBAC rules.

The fix joins all remaining path segments with `strings.Join(pathSplit[8:], "/")`. `portforward` is special-cased because its trailing segments (`{port}`, `{protocol}`) are dynamic path parameters, not part of the subresource name.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The change is minimal and self-contained in two files for easy backporting.

{"author": "person-6815db69", "base": "main", "body": "TDX provides Secure Boot through a stateless OVMF firmware with embedded keys (OVMF.inteltdx.secboot.fd), which does not rely on SMM for UEFI variable protection. However, Proj unconditionally required SMM when Secure Boot was enabled, making TDX + Secure Boot impossible to configure.

This change:
- Exempts TDX VMs from the "SecureBoot requires SMM" validation
- Sets SecureLoader=false for TDX in the domain XML to avoid libvirt's own SMM requirement when secure="yes" is set
- Adds a test for TDX + SecureBoot without SMM

The existing rejection of TDX + SMM is preserved.

disks proceed to the expansion path.

{"author": "person-ec225de8", "base": "main", "body": "VMIs based on the MSHV hypervisor take longer to be deleted. 60 seconds timeout is not enough at times, which causes flakiness in the test. 120 seconds has been seen to be sufficient.

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

The test case `[sig-compute]VMI with external kernel boot with external alpine-based kernel only (without initrd) ensure successful boot and deletion when VMI has a disk defined` in `tests/component-757` expects the VMI to be deleted within 60 seconds, otherwise the test fails. On MSHV hypervisor, VM takes much longer than KVM, causing the timeout to be violated. This results in flakiness in the test.

#### After this PR:

The timeout is increased to 120 seconds, which is high enough for both KVM and MSHV. The test consistently passes.
